summary: Validated non-blocking geo currency prefill on POST /api/auth/register (iteration 891). 8/8 pytest cases PASS. UK signup (X-Forwarded-For=81.2.69.142) → user.currency_preference resolves to 'GBP' within ~1-2s via /api/auth/me (polled). Private-IP signup (10.0.0.5) → currency_preference stays null (USD default preserved). Benin signup (154.66.135.1) → currency_preference='XOF'. Manual override wins: PUT /api/auth/profile with currency_preference=CAD on the UK user persists to CAD and is returned by /auth/me — the guard filter {currency_preference: {$in: [null, '']}} correctly prevents the background prefill from overwriting a user-chosen value. Regressions confirmed: duplicate email → 400, weak password → 400, rate limit 5/hour is still active (observed 429 within 6 rapid attempts). /api/geo/detect anonymous public endpoint still returns 200 with correct GB/GBP mapping. Registration latency measured at ~1.6s (welcome + verification emails included) — geo prefill runs on a fire-and-forget asyncio task and does NOT block the response.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/auth.py L1767-1768: _prefill_asyncio.create_task(...) is fire-and-forget with no add_done_callback for exception surfacing (only the inner try/except logs). A stronger pattern already exists two functions below (_schedule_non_blocking_task at L1849) which attaches add_done_callback for guarded logging. Consider using it here for consistency (currently the inner try/except is broad, so this is cosmetic — no runtime impact observed).

routes/auth.py L1748: `country = await detect_country_from_ip(ip)` is called even when ip is 'unknown'; detect_country_from_ip already treats that as private→'US' so no harm, but flagging that the elif branch will then write signup_country='US' for users we couldn't geolocate at all — that's fine but worth documenting.

routes/auth.py L1755-1756: the elif clause fires for ANY resolved country whose currency isn't supported OR is USD, and stores signup_country. This includes private IPs (US) and unsupported-currency countries — good UX signal for analytics.

routes/geo_detection.py COUNTRIES map: PL (PLN) and TH (THB) still missing from previous iteration 890's finding. Not related to this iteration, but visitors from Poland/Thailand who sign up will get signup_country=PL/TH (nice) but no currency_preference because currency is falsy for those countries (they're not in COUNTRIES). Same 91% coverage gap noted in iteration 890 still holds. LOW priority.

PUT /api/auth/profile (L7990) accepts arbitrary currency_preference string with only .upper() normalization — no validation against SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES set. A client could set currency_preference='ZZZ' and it would persist. Consider adding: `if request.currency_preference.upper() not in SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES: raise HTTPException(400, ...)`. Not blocking this iteration but worth an enhancement ticket.

Signup response body (L1820-1827) does NOT include currency_preference or signup_country; the frontend must call /auth/me after register to see the prefilled currency. Acceptable because prefill is async, but if the frontend wants to reflect the geo-detected currency immediately in a post-signup toast/UI without polling, consider returning `signup_country_hint` in the register response (based on synchronous geo lookup) — future enhancement, not a bug.
